text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HAARETZ
- Army chief of staff: 3.5 billion shekels ($1 billion) needed to prepare army for war in light of Syrian threat.
- Senior Egyptian army officers toured near border with Israel in violation of 1979 peace treaty.
- 1997 budget totalling 190.8 billion shekels tabled in parliament.
- U.S. tries to set up summit between Palestinian President Arafat and Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu.
- Ministerial committee decides to freeze bringing in foreign workers and to deport 500 illegal workers per month.
- Head of religious education authority slams media over reporting on segments of the population.
JERUSALEM POST
- Clinton presses for Hebron Israeli redeployment pact.
- Hebron Jewish leaders 'very worried' after meeting Netanyahu on impending redeployment.
- Netanyahu: Syrians won't surprise us.
- Treasury: More cuts may be necessary in 1997 budget.
- Insurers agree to pay fines in price fixing case.
- Clal Industries backs out of Yotvata daily company purchase.
MAARIV
- Director general of treasury warns to expect "dangerous" economic year.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Flaws in security against suicide bombings on public transportation: during certain hours there is no guarding.
- Granddaughter of Nazi Goebbels, identified only by initials, converted to Judaism, married Jewish descendant of Holocaust survivors, lives in Germany.
GLOBES
- Treasury director general says economy entering complicated and dangerous situation in wake of peace process stagnation and real revaluation.
